Overview

GNPS is an open web ecosystem for community analysis, organization, searching, annotation, and sharing of tandem mass-spectrometry data. It hosts spectral libraries and multiple analysis workflows, including molecular networking and repository-scale search, and interoperates with public MassIVE datasets and structured sample metadata.

Detailed capability map

What can this tool do?

Spectral-library matchingRepository-scale spectral searchMetadata-based contextualizationNetwork visualizationProvenance tracking

Common uses

  • Search experimental MS/MS spectra against community spectral libraries.
  • Build classical or feature-based molecular networks.
  • Share datasets, libraries, workflows, and analysis results with collaborators or the public.

Scope and considerations

Designed for

  • MS/MS-centered annotation, molecular networking, public-data search, and community sharing of metabolomics and natural-products data.

Important requirements

  • Most workflows require centroided/open mass-spectrometry formats and appropriate metadata or feature tables for the selected analysis.

Considerations

  • GNPS is an ecosystem rather than a single algorithm; users should cite and report the specific workflow, version or task URL used.
